title: test-0124-GEN-ONLINESAFETY
passage: In the digital age, protecting your online identity requires constant vigilance. Many students mistakenly believe that using a single strong password for all accounts is sufficient, but this practice is dangerous because a breach in one site compromises your entire digital life. Similarly, never share your One-Time Password (OTP) with anyone, even if the caller claims to be from your bank and knows your personal details. Genuine financial institutions never ask for your OTP over the phone. Furthermore, be cautious of phishing attempts; a message might look professional with a company logo, but it could still be a malicious trap designed to steal your data. Remember that online actions have lasting consequences. Even if you delete a post or message, it may have already been saved or screenshotted by others, meaning it is never truly gone from the internet. Finally, do not assume that using Incognito mode makes you invisible. While it prevents your browser from saving history, your internet service provider and the websites you visit can still track your activity. Always practice critical thinking, as online safety is not just about technology, but about the habits you build to protect your privacy and reputation.
summary: In the digital age, protecting your online identity requires constant vigilance. Always practice critical thinking, because online safety isn't just about using technology—it's about building habits to protect your privacy and reputation.
